channel.title: mint - news
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: Did Ilhan Omar marry her brother for a marriage-based green card? What’s the investigation about? Explained
item.description: Federal investigators are reportedly examining allegations that Ilhan Omar committed immigration fraud and misrepresented her age during her father’s naturalisation process.&nbsp;

item.title: Not getting involved: JD Vance opts out of endorsing Netanyahu as Israel PM warns of future ‘hostile’ US president
item.description: JD Vance refuses to back Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s election as the Israeli prime minister warns of a potentially hostile future US president.

item.title: Bomb threat delays Chennai-Goa IndiGo flight by 5 hours, says report: Here's what happened
item.description: IndiGo flight 6E588 was scheduled to take off at 5.40 pm on Monday. But a bomb threat reportedly delayed the take-off.

item.title: Kim Jong Un dead? North Korea releases ‘proof of life’ photos of Supreme Leader after 'brain hemorrhage' rumors
item.description: The images shared by North Korean state media KCNA and NK News showed leader Kim Jong Un inspecting shoes and women’s clothing.

item.title: Trump thanks ‘legendary’ friend Elon Musk for pledging SpaceX shares to every American child through Trump Accounts
item.description: Donald Trump thanked Elon Musk for pledging one SpaceX share to every American child next year through Trump Accounts. The proposed donation could be worth about $10.7 billion, though details of how the shares will be distributed remain unclear.

item.title: Dussehra-Vijayadashami 2026 wishes family, friends and colleagues; WhatsApp status: Celebrate triumph of good over evil
item.description: Dussehra, also known as Vijayadashami, celebrates the triumph of good over evil. While many regions mark Lord Rama’s victory over Ravana, parts of eastern India celebrate Goddess Durga’s victory over Mahishasura.&nbsp;

item.title: Links to Saudi royal family, plans to leave US: What filing against ex-OpenAI engineer who planted device revealed
item.description: Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, accused of planting a recording device in an executive meeting room, was in contact with a Saudi royal and planned to leave the US, prosecutors said. A judge denied bail over concerns he could flee.

item.title: Saudi Arabia delays investor summit to 2027 amid Houthi attacks: S&P Global’s Yergin says, ‘reasonable decision'
item.description: Saudi Arabia postpones its Future Investment Initiative until 2027 as Houthi missile and drone attacks raise security concerns for investors.

item.title: Trai plans uniform OTP format to curb scams
item.description: Trai is discussing uniform OTP SMS formats with telecom operators and may issue a consultation paper. Standard templates could make messages easier to recognize and prevent codes appearing in previews, but experts caution that consistency alone will not stop scams.&nbsp;

item.title: Daylight Saving Time 2026: 1-hour clock change on November 1, 301-117 House vote and Senate roadblock — 3 things to know
item.description: Daylight saving time (DST) ends at 2 am local time on Sunday, November 1, when clocks move back to 1 am.

item.title: 1 war, 2 disease outbreaks, 1 oil crisis: 6 countries face higher risks, 3 see lower risks — Inside 2027 Global Risk Map
item.description: The ongoing conflict with the US and Israel, economic challenges, and arbitrary detentions have raised Iran’s risk rating from High to Extreme.&nbsp;

item.title: Italy protests: Indian nationals in Italy advised to exercise caution, avoid crowded areas
item.description: The advisory comes as shops in central Milan closed early on Monday, fearing another wave of unrest after two days of protests in which demonstrators clashed with police, looted stores and vandalised property.

item.title: UK says it has no record of Bhopal merchant’s 109-year-old ₹35,000 British war bond investment: What MP family claims
item.description: The UK’s Debt Management Office says it found no evidence of a 1917 ₹35,000 Indian War Loan allegedly subscribed by a Bhopal merchant. His Madhya Pradesh family is seeking clarity on whether the investment was repaid, with the century-old claim still unresolved.

item.title: Air India, IndiGo, AAIB to face parliamentary panel on November 2 for aviation sector review
item.description: A parliamentary committee led by Baijayant Panda will meet Air India, IndiGo and aviation safety and security officials on November 2 to review the performance of civil aviation public-sector undertakings.

item.title: Andre Agassi, Steffi Graf sold their $23 million California mansion at a big loss in 2006 — What happened?
item.description: Their 2006 sale of their luxury mansion remains a striking example of how even an exceptional property, owned by two global sports stars, can require substantial price cuts before finding a buyer.

item.title: FSSAI warns nutraceutical firms over labelling violations, threatens action for non-compliance
item.description: FSSAI warns against violation of mandatory labelling norms for nutraceuticals, health supplements

item.title: River cleanup activist Bittu Tabahi is upset after one dustbin is stolen; he kept it near river— Check his video message
item.description: Tabahi shared a video on Instagram showing he had placed two dustbins near the riverbank to encourage people to dispose of their waste properly. However, when he returned to the spot, he found that one of the bins was stolen.

item.title: Govt curbs sugar diversion for ethanol, mills warn of losses during surplus year
item.description: State-run oil marketing companies have excluded ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from their latest procurement tender for the 2026-27 supply year for petrol blending, prompting mills to urge the Centre to retain these feedstocks in future procurement cycles.

item.title: Ex-Chief of Air Staff of Bangladesh Air Force arrested: Who is Sheikh Abdul Hannan? What Interpol notified?
item.description: The former air chief is accused of accumulating assets beyond his known sources of income and conducting suspicious financial transactions through multiple bank accounts.

item.title: India-New Zealand FTA to come into force on 20 Oct: Piyush Goyal
item.description: The agreement is part of India's efforts to strike bilateral deals to push exports at a time when geopolitical conflicts have intensified and global supply-chains are getting realigned.

item.title: Mumbai airport impasse persists as Adani insists on airline capacity curbs
item.description: Airlines maintain they have not agreed to shift international operations to Navi Mumbai or surrender their slots at the Mumbai airport.

item.title: Nepal bans India-made Priyagold biscuits after FSSAI flags food safety violations
item.description: Issuing a notice on Monday, the Food Technology and Quality Control Department of Nepal imposed restrictions on import, sales, and distribution of Priya Gold biscuits manufactured by India's Surya Food and Agro Ltd, describing the product as sub-standard.

item.title: How IIT Guwahati student Uditansh Raghuvanshi discovered a passion for javelin beyond academics
item.description: While his parents and grandfather helped others learn through teaching, Raghuvanshi believes his own experience with athletics and sports administration has helped him develop a similar instinct to create opportunities for others.

item.title: Why Delhi Police’s ₹15.7-crore facial recognition CCTV tender is facing scrutiny amid CJP protests: Concerns explained
item.description: Delhi Police’s ₹15.7-crore tender for 338 surveillance cameras with facial recognition technology has drawn scrutiny over privacy safeguards, data retention and alleged procurement flaws. The concerns come amid CJP protests, though no evidence links the tender directly to the demonstrations.

item.title: Kolkata’s rainbow-painted Chingrighata flyover raises road-safety concerns: What IIT expert says about skidding risks
item.description: According to the expert, motorcycles are more vulnerable to reduced surface friction because they have lower stability and a smaller tyre contact area.

item.title: ED raids Mumbai, Ahmedabad and other cities in alleged ₹200 crore 'pump-and-dump' share manipulation case
item.description: The Enforcement Directorate froze ₹200 crore in trading accounts during searches at 20 locations across Maharashtra and Gujarat in an alleged pump-and-dump share manipulation case. The agency also seized documents, digital devices, share transaction records and property documents.

item.title: Israel-made nets offer apple growers a shield from hail hit
item.description: Anti-hail nets now cover a growing share of Himachal Pradesh’s apple orchards, offering farmers a defence against storms that can devastate a harvest. But installation is a significant investment, even with government subsidies.&nbsp;

item.title: Inside UP’s 1,000-acre data centre hub plan in Bundelkhand: Location, land and investment incentives explained
item.description: Uttar Pradesh plans a 1,000-acre data centre and IT hub near Jhansi in Bundelkhand, with 810 acres assembled so far. Here’s what the plan covers, where the hub will come up, the infrastructure required and the incentives available to attract investors.

item.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Zelenskyy seeks India’s help to reopen Black Sea grain route — why Delhi’s role matters
item.description: Ukraine is holding talks with India, Turkey and Egypt to restore safe navigation in the Black Sea and resume grain exports, but Russia has resisted the proposal. New Delhi’s ties with Moscow and Kyiv and its peace framework put the diplomatic role in focus.

item.title: FSSAI proposes ban on added sugars in infant foods: Why it wants to act and how sucrose, fructose can harm babies
item.description: FSSAI has proposed banning sucrose and fructose in foods for infants up to six months, aiming to limit early exposure to added sugars and support age-appropriate nutrition. Details here.

item.title: Firing on Tiger Shroff: Big catch! Who are Rehan alias Sukka, Hritik Kurmi alias Roshan and a minor - 3 primary suspects
item.description: Rajasthan Police arrested three suspects in the Tiger Shroff firing case aboard the Pune–Jaipur Express in Kota following inputs from Mumbai Police. The accused, including two adults and a minor, were allegedly trying to flee to Nepal via Delhi.

item.title: Who is Anil Pandit? Gangster linked to Tiger Shroff shooting case who asked Salman Khan to apologise to Bishnoi — report
item.description: Tiger Shroff shooting case: The Delhi Police said preliminary questioning revealed that one of the suspected shooters, named Rehan (18), was in communication with Anil Pandit.

item.title: $592 million dividend payout - Here's how this Dubai firm is attracting investors in UAE's first IPO after Iran war
item.description: DIP Holding plans $592 million in dividends over three years to attract investors to the UAE’s first IPO of 2026. Dubai Investments will sell a 20% stake, with subscriptions opening on October 27, as the Iran war weighs on Gulf markets.

item.title: India-US trade deal ‘very close’ to completion, Marco Rubio says ahead of Mumbai, Jamnagar visit
item.description: Rubio said that every country has a complex set of factors that it has to take into account. 'Geography is real. For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources. That's not an excuse, but all of that has to be balanced when making foreign policy,' he added.

item.title: Who is 2024-batch IPS officer Kuhu Garg? Former No. 1 international badminton player wins ‘Sword of Honour’ in Hyderabad
item.description: Before choosing civil services, Kuhu Garg had an impressive career representing India on the global badminton circuit from 2013 to 2020. She was coached by Dr D.K. Sen and later by Padma Bhushan awardee Pullela Gopichand at the Pullela Gopichand Academy in Hyderabad.
